explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem is one node in a computer-generated certificate. It claims that `RowSquare` holds for two specific partitions (lists of natural numbers). `RowSquare` is the library's own abbreviation, `SquareOccurs (rowDiagram p) (rowDiagram q)`, defined in `UniversalSquare/Support/RowSquareTools.lean`; going by the folder name, it is about a shape occurring in a tensor square. The proof joins two earlier certificate nodes (`sg18913`, `sg19969`) using the library lemma `rowSquare_join`. All of the content lives in the library's own definitions and certificates. Mathlib has no notion of `RowSquare`, `SquareOccurs` or `rowDiagram`, and nothing that would settle this particular pair of partitions.
